title: safety-belt-refactor-playbook-scratch
content:
Context and motivation:
- Working on a medium-risk refactor: split out request routing safety checks and introduce a 'safety-belt' wrapper around route handlers (goal: reduce blast radius when changing batching/routing logic).
- Need a lightweight playbook to keep PR reviews fast but safe: small diff surfaces, test coverage, canary gating, rollback plan, and explicit observability hooks.

High-level goals for this patch series:
1) Make the change incrementally deployable with feature flag gating.
2) Add non-intrusive telemetry for every incoming request path (counts, latencies, error types).
3) Ensure any degradation triggers automatic fallback to the previous routing path.
4) Keep token-level cost impact < 2% for median workloads.

Design notes / nudges:
- Safety-belt wrapper = decorator that: 1) validates input shape, 2) tracks KV-cache hits/misses for prefix cache, 3) enforces a per-request timeout and fallback to legacy handler.
- Implement as a thin interface so we can flip on/off via config map without touching core runtime logic.
- No changes to model kernels or quantization paths in this PR — keep scope focused to routing and orchestration.

PR checklist (pre-review):
- [ ] Diff size: keep < 400 LOC across 2–3 files if possible. If larger, split into a follow-up.
- [ ] Feature flag guard around new code paths (env + console toggle).
- [ ] Unit tests for safety-belt wrapper: happy path, validation error, KV-cache miss path, fallback invocation.
- [ ] Integration test (local): synthetic workload that simulates bursty small prompts + long prompts.
- [ ] e2e smoke with batching disabled / enabled to ensure consistent behavior.
- [ ] Add metrics (names & tags documented in PR body): routing.safety_belt.invocations, routing.safety_belt.fallbacks, routing.safety_belt.latency_ms (p50/p95), routing.safety_belt.kv_miss_rate.
- [ ] Add structured logs: include request_id, route_name, safety_belt_version, fallback_reason.
- [ ] Update runbook snippets for oncall (how to flip feature flag, impact assessment, rollback steps).
- [ ] Add a short performance micro-benchmark: median token latency before/after (attach raw numbers in PR).

Review guidance for reviewers:
- Keep focus on correctness, observability, and rollbackability. Prefer small changes over clever abstractions.
- If you see any place where the wrapper can mask upstream errors (e.g., catch-and-swallow), call it out — prefer explicit fallback reasons with metrics so we can decode behavior in prod.
- Validate that the added metrics use the same cardinality patterns we use elsewhere (avoid high-cardinality labels on per-request user data).

Canary plan (staging -> prod):
1) Deploy to staging (safety_belt: on) for 24h, run automated load generator (50k requests, mixture of short/long prompts). Verify no error spike and kv_miss_rate within expectations.
2) Canary: 1% traffic to safety-belt in prod for 6 hours. Observe: error rate, p95 latency, fallback ratio, token cost delta.
3) Ramp to 10% for 2h if metrics stable.
4) Ramp to 50% if stable, then 100% after overnight observation.

Canary metrics and thresholds (initial proposal):
- error_rate: must not exceed baseline + 0.5% absolute.
- p95 latency: must not degrade > 10% relative.
- fallback_ratio: <= 1% initially, investigate if > 0.5% in staging.
- kv_miss_rate: no more than 3x baseline (we expect a small bump during rollout).
- token_cost_delta: median increase < 2% (if > 2% stop and investigate).

Rollback plan (fast):
- Flip feature flag to off via console or CLI; operability steps in runbook.
- If flag flip fails, redeploy previous revision (record last-green commit id in runbook).
- Postmortem checklist: collect 1) runbook timeline, 2) suspect request examples, 3) metric dashboards, 4) logs with request_id and safety_belt_version.

Post-merge follow-ups (next PRs / TODOs):
- A: Add adaptive batching knob that the safety-belt can suggest to router when under high contention.
- B: Move telemetry tags to shared constants (avoid copy/paste across modules).
- C: Backfill integration tests into CI for the synthetic workload used during canary.
- D: Explore small-memory LRU for prefix cache used by safety-belt (measure memory vs hit-rate).

Potential risks & mitigation ideas (notes to self):
- Risk: safety-belt adds tail latency for cold requests.
  Mitigation: short-circuit path for requests with existing prefix KV hits; add early exit profiling.
- Risk: high-cardinality logs/metrics leak PII.
  Mitigation: sanitize request metadata; avoid user ids in metric tags.
- Risk: behavioral divergence between safety-belt and legacy handler causing subtle output diffs for some prompts.
  Mitigation: add a small A/B eval harness comparing outputs on a fixed prompt set (1000 prompts) and surface quality regressions before broad rollouts.

Notes for PR body (copy/paste checklist):
- Short summary (what, why).
- Scope and non-goals (explicitly say what this PR does NOT change).
- How to test locally (commands + env vars).
- Metrics added (names + dashboard links).
- Canary plan and rollback steps.
- Size/complexity justification.
- Request reviewers: @kai, @noelle, @soren (ops perspective).

Quick local commands (draft - update if paths change):
- run unit tests: ./tools/test -k safety_belt
- run integration: ./tools/integration-run --scenario safety-belt-local --duration 5m
- generate load: ./tools/loadgen --profile small-plus-large --qps 200 --target staging

Open questions (need opinion from Kai / Noelle):
- Should the safety-belt be a route decorator or a middleware in the dispatcher layer? Middleware is easier for cross-cutting telemetry, but decorator gives per-route fine-grained control.
- What should the default fallback policy be? Simple 'call legacy handler' vs queue-and-retry. I prefer legacy handler for predictability.

Short todo (me):
- [ ] Draft PR and include runbook snippet.
- [ ] Add basic unit tests.
- [ ] Wire up metrics and push small dashboard.
- [ ] Kick off staging canary once PR is merged behind flag.

Random brain dump (keep here for later):
- Could use an opt-in header to annotate certain traffic (internal test traffic) so we can run noisier experiments without affecting customer signals.
- If fallback becomes common, we should track root causes (misrouted model version? insufficient batching window?) and create a small incident taxonomy.

------
Small log of current experiments (keep track):
- 2025-02-12: prototype decorator implementation, measured median token latency change +0.4% on local runner. KV miss rate up ~1.3x.
- 2025-02-14: added timeout guard and fallback hook; local integration saw one fallback per 5k requests (acceptable).
- 2025-02-16: ran small A/B on 1k prompt set — output diffs: 4 samples flagged as 'quality regression' — need manual inspection before canary.

End of scratchpad.
